digest:
The day’s papers weave a rich tapestry around holographic dualities, higher‑point dynamics, and the geometry of conformal blocks.  On the holography front, several works push the boundary of AdS/CFT: the exact surface‑defect bootstrap in “Surface defects in μ=4 SYM” delivers closed‑form two‑point functions of chiral primaries in the presence of a half‑BPS defect, matching both weak‑coupling expansions and a Witten‑diagram bootstrap on the rotation‑invariant locus.  In flat‑space holography, the construction of quantum gravity from unstable D‑branes in “Quantum Gravity in Asymptotically Flat Spacetimes from Unstable D-Branes” realizes a flat‑space analogue of holography by mapping closed‑string excitations to gauge‑invariant OSFT operators, reproducing the full closed‑string S‑matrix perturbatively.  The study of horizon symmetries in “Horizon symmetries of exact hydrodynamic actions” further links diffeomorphisms preserving black‑hole horizons to effective hydrodynamic actions, illuminating the role of gauge symmetries in maximal chaos.  Complementing these, “Reconstruction of Black Hole Islands from Hawking Radiation via the Algebraic Petz Map” provides a rigorous algebraic Petz‑map construction that reproduces the island formula, while “Extremal black hole mimickers: geometry, stability, and long‑delay signal trains” offers a horizonless spacetime that mimics extremal black holes, shedding light on echo phenomenology and stability in AdS/CFT contexts.

Higher‑point and conformal‑block themes also dominate: “All‑multiplicity completion of maximally supersymmetric gauge amplitudes” shows that six‑point constraints uniquely fix the derivative expansion for any multiplicity, using KLT bilinears and sphere integrals to build local, factorizing tree amplitudes—an elegant demonstration that higher‑point consistency follows from lower‑point data.  The energy‑energy correlator in “The hidden sunrise in the energy‑energy correlator” completes the NNLO calculation by uncovering an elliptic sector tied to the γ1(6) modular curve, expressed via iterated Eisenstein integrals and opening a new window on Landau singularities.  In the realm of null‑string dynamics, “Carroll‑Weyl gauged null strings in AdS” derives a radial‑adapted BMS$_3$ algebra with a weight‑one current, revealing a novel anomaly structure and a critical dimension $D=27$ for highest‑weight representations.  Together, these papers underscore a vibrant interplay between holographic bootstrap, higher‑point amplitudes, and the algebraic structure of conformal blocks, offering fresh tools and insights for anyone exploring the frontiers of holography, celestial amplitudes, and beyond.

papers.title: Closed Universe, Quantum Entanglement and Observers
papers.authors: Hao Geng
papers.abstract: It has been argued that in quantum gravity the Hilbert space associated with any closed universe is trivially one-dimensional. To reconcile this argument with the richness of our own universe, it was suggested that a nontrivial Hilbert space will emerge once an ``observer" is included. Such an ``observer" has been modeled in different ways. There are three concrete classes of models: $\textbf{1)}$ The ``observer" is modeled by a term in the full Hamiltonian of the system which is linear in a phase space variable; $\textbf{2)}$ The ``observer" is modeled in the quantum circuit model of holography as a subsystem in the closed universe which is entangled with an external non-gravitational system; $\textbf{3)}$ The ``observer" is argued to be described by the emergent Goldstone bosons when the diffeomorphisms are spontaneously broken. In fact, the third class was discovered by an attempt to physically realize the first class. In this paper, we will show that the second class can also be unified into the third class. Our result indicates that the emergence of the ``observer" is a manifestation of the $\textit{Massive Islands}$ paradigm. It demonstrates that the graviton mass is a feature of the quantum state. One should think of the islands as closed universes and the Goldstone boson associated with the graviton mass as the ``observer", which is exactly the case at late-times for evaporating black holes. An implication of this work is that the ``observer" can ``observe" global symmetries in quantum gravity.
papers.summary: This paper argues that a nontrivial Hilbert space for a closed universe emerges when an observer is included, unifying three observer models and linking the phenomenon to the Massive Islands paradigm and graviton mass. It suggests that observers correspond to Goldstone bosons associated with spontaneously broken diffeomorphisms, implying that observers can detect global symmetries in quantum gravity.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of interacting magnetic chain molecules
papers.authors: Alexios P. Polychronakos, Konstantinos Sfetsos
papers.abstract: We study magnets composed of molecules with an arbitrary number $m$ of magnetically active atoms in a chain configuration interacting with nearest-neighbor couplings. We derive the thermodynamics of a chain of spin-$j$ $SU(2)$ magnetic atoms using a mean-field approach and determine the equilibrium states and stability conditions. The system exhibits a rich phase structure with a cascade of ferromagnetic phase transitions, their number ranging from $m$, for maximal ferromagnets, to zero, for paramagnets, depending on the relative strengths of the couplings. In the presence of impurities (modified couplings) at the ends of the chain, boundary states emerge that coexist with the paramagnetic phase or the fully ferromagnetic phase. For long chains, a continuum approximation can be taken that clarifies the structure of the phases. In the continuum description, magnetized states at temperatures lower than the critical temperature at which they appear correspond to kink solitons.
papers.summary: The authors analyze spin‑j SU(2) magnetic chains with nearest‑neighbor couplings using a mean‑field approach, uncovering a cascade of ferromagnetic phase transitions whose number depends on the coupling hierarchy. Impurities at chain ends generate boundary states that coexist with paramagnetic or fully ferromagnetic phases, and in the long‑chain limit a continuum description reveals kink soliton solutions below the critical temperature.

papers.title: Prescriptive Master Integrals of Maximal Weight at Two Loops
papers.authors: Jacob L. Bourjaily
papers.abstract: We describe the construction of a spanning set of individually pure, planar master integrals involving massless particles in four dimensions which include all maximal-weight contributions at two loops. In this basis, every independent region associated with infrared divergence is individually matched by specific masters, with all other masters being manifestly finite in four dimensions.
papers.summary: The paper constructs a basis of pure, planar two-loop master integrals for massless particles in four dimensions, ensuring each infrared-divergent region is matched by a specific master while all others remain finite. This framework provides a systematic way to isolate maximal-weight contributions, facilitating precise amplitude computations in perturbative quantum field theory.

papers.title: Gluons and Knots
papers.authors: Alfredo Guevara
papers.abstract: We argue that the scattering amplitude of a single minus helicity gluon with arbitrarily many positive helicity gluons is topological. The amplitude is constant in chambers of kinematic space, its resonances are located at walls and its factorization is determined by wall-crossing. Yangian invariance dictates the amplitude to be determined by a 2d null Wilson loop that can be lifted into a positive and transverse 3d link. By reinterpreting wall-crossing and the Weinberg soft theorem as skein relations and Reidemeister moves of the subknots, we construct a state-counting description consisting of adding the `corners' of their HOMFLY-PT polynomials. Beyond the classical limit, we argue that this provides a conjectured but precise connection to topological field and string theory.   The new formula is rigorously derived via a Lean-formalized dependency graph (DAG) as detailed in a companion paper, laying out the precise assumptions including Reidemeister III invariance. It is further tested exhaustively, including novel `star' kinematics where the amplitude and state count are shown to become Catalan numbers, in agreement with knot theory literature.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the all‑plus helicity gluon amplitude with one negative helicity is a topological invariant, constant in kinematic chambers and governed by wall‑crossing encoded as knot skein relations. It connects Yangian symmetry, 2d Wilson loops, and HOMFLY‑PT polynomials, offering a conjectural link to topological field theory and string theory.

papers.title: Hawking Amplitudes: Subtle Points About Saddle Points
papers.authors: Owen Lear, Daniel McLoughlin, Sebastian Mizera, John Staunton
papers.abstract: Hawking amplitudes provide a new way of determining the Hawking spectrum of black holes, using on-shell techniques borrowed from the literature on scattering amplitudes. In this paper, we investigate the interplay between the semi-classical and weak-field approximations previously used to compute Hawking amplitudes. We find that these limits do not necessarily commute, highlighting subtleties with the saddle point analyses governing the semi-classical limit. Resolving these issues allows us to compute semi-classical Hawking amplitudes in a range of black-hole backgrounds, including Tangherlini, Reissner-Nordstr\"om, and Hernquist metrics. Moreover, we describe the saddle-point contributions dominating Hawking amplitudes for different energies and propose a new method for determining the temperature of the resulting thermal spectrum based on Stokes lines of Hawking amplitudes.
papers.summary: This work develops on-shell methods to compute Hawking radiation amplitudes, revealing non‑commutativity between semi‑classical and weak‑field limits and clarifying saddle‑point contributions across various black‑hole geometries. It also proposes a novel Stokes‑line technique to extract the Hawking temperature from the amplitude structure.

papers.title: Covariant BCFW for All Masses
papers.authors: Jacob L. Bourjaily, Michael Plesser
papers.abstract: We use the massive spinor-helicity formalism to describe a novel construction for massive spinors which allows one to connect the many choices of bases useful in the representation of amplitudes involving massive particles, and we use this to derive a new formulation for the general BCFW shift that is valid regardless whether or which of the particles involved are massive or massless. This formalism should help facilitate a more coherent implementation of on-shell recursion for computing amplitudes involving massive particles in four dimensions.
papers.summary: This paper develops a covariant BCFW shift that works for any combination of massive and massless particles using the massive spinor-helicity formalism, enabling on-shell recursion in four dimensions. It offers a unified framework that could streamline the computation of higher-point scattering amplitudes involving massive states.

papers.title: General Spin-1 Dynamics During Inflation: Microcausality Constraints and Cosmological Collider Signals
papers.authors: Trevor Cheung, Carlos Duaso-Pueyo, David Stefanyszyn, Dong-Gang Wang
papers.abstract: We construct the general theory of a spin-1 field propagating on an inflationary background consistent with scale invariance, rotations, Bunch-Davies conditions and microcausality. Our Boostless Proca theory generalises the usual massive Proca theory to a Lagrangian with 5 free parameters: 4 corresponding to parity-even terms and a single parity-odd term. We impose three degrees of freedom from the outset and find that microcausality, the statement that field operators vanish outside the lightcone, requires the kinetic terms to be gauge invariant. We couple this spin-1 state to the inflaton and study the signatures it imprints on cosmological correlators. We find no new signals for the bispectrum meaning that the known signals are the most general thereby providing a very clean model-independent probe of new physics in this leading form of non-Gaussianity. For the trispectrum and higher-point functions, the boostless Proca theory produces new shapes with all 5 parameters in principle measurable.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a general spin‑1 theory on an inflationary background that respects scale invariance, rotations, Bunch‑Davies vacuum, and microcausality, leading to a boost‑less Proca Lagrangian with five free parameters. It shows that while the bispectrum remains unchanged, the trispectrum and higher‑point correlators acquire new shapes that could be probed in cosmological collider experiments.

papers.title: Scattering entanglement entropy between one particle species and the others
papers.authors: Yuan-Hao Zheng, Jiayin Gu
papers.abstract: We construct the entanglement entropy of a general scattering process between one particle species (denoted as $A$) and the rest of the final state. Assuming a pure initial momentum eigenstate, we show that the reduced density matrix in particle $A$'s Fock space is block-diagonal in zero-, one- and multi-particle states, and is diagonal in the momentum basis for the one-particle state. As a result, we could write down the Von Neumann entropy of particle $A$, $S_A$, in terms of scattering probabilities and differential cross sections, assuming no more than one particle $A$ is produced in the final state. $S_A$ contains the information of both the total scattering probabilities (or cross sections) and the differential distributions --- the latter depends on a phase-space resolution factor as a result of the infinite-dimensional momentum Hilbert space. Our result is general and model-independent since we consider the full final state from time evolution ($S|i\rangle$) rather than a specific outcome, and is applicable as long as the probability for producing multiple particle $A$ is subleading. We also obtain the $n\geq2$ Tsallis and R\'enyi entropies in our framework and find out that, at the leading order, they are proportional to the total scattering probability and carry no differential information.
papers.summary: The authors derive a general expression for the entanglement entropy of a single particle species in a scattering process, showing that the reduced density matrix is block‑diagonal and diagonal in the one‑particle momentum basis. They express the Von Neumann entropy in terms of scattering probabilities and differential cross sections, and also compute Tsallis and Rényi entropies, finding them proportional to the total scattering probability at leading order.

papers.title: Large Charge Jets in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM Energy Correlators
papers.authors: Alba Grassi, Cristoforo Iossa, Luigi Tizzano, Alexander Zhiboedov
papers.abstract: We compute the energy-energy correlator in a state created by a heavy canonical operator of scaling dimension $\Delta_H$ in $\mathcal{N}=4$ $SU(N)$ SYM, at fixed $N$ and arbitrary values of the large charge 't Hooft coupling $\lambda \sim \Delta_H g_{\rm YM}^2$. The state created by the canonical operator triggers spontaneous breaking of conformal symmetry and the Higgs mechanism, with squared W-boson masses proportional to $\lambda$. We start with the known finite-coupling result for the underlying four-point function of local operators, perform the detector and Fourier transforms and express the resulting energy-energy correlator as an infinite OPE sum in the source-detector channel, which we then analyze both numerically and analytically. We show that the finite-coupling energy-energy correlator exhibits a hierarchy of distinct physical regimes as a function of $z=(1-\cos\theta)/2$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the detectors. A small-angle vacuum-dominated behavior at $z\ll\lambda^{-1}$ is followed by a non-monotonic medium-induced transient behavior at $\lambda z \sim1$. A large charge jet regime follows, where the energy-energy correlator displays a power-law behavior $\sim1/(\lambda z^3)$ for $\lambda^{-1}\lesssim z \lesssim \lambda^{-1/3}$, before approaching an angle-independent plateau at larger angles.
papers.summary: The paper computes the energy-energy correlator for a heavy operator in μ=4 SYM at arbitrary large ’t Hooft coupling, revealing a hierarchy of angular regimes—from vacuum-dominated small angles to a jet-like power-law and an angle-independent plateau. It does so by performing detector and Fourier transforms on the finite-coupling four-point function, expressing the result as an infinite OPE sum in the source–detector channel and analyzing it numerically and analytically.

papers.title: Reconstructing BPS String Charge Cone in 6d N=(1,0) Supergravity
papers.authors: Yuta Hamada, Hee-Cheol Kim, Kai Xu
papers.abstract: The tensor branch of six-dimensional $\mathcal N=(1,0)$ supergravity is characterized by a spectrum of BPS strings charged under the two-form gauge fields. Their charges span a cone in the tensor charge lattice, whose extremal rays are generated by primitive BPS string charges that become tensionless at the boundaries of the tensor moduli space. We develop a systematic procedure, based entirely on effective field theory data, to reconstruct the primitive BPS string generators and thereby determine the complete closed BPS string cone of any 6d $(1,0)$ supergravity theory. The key ingredients are the universal {\it H}-string, which allows us to isolate a fixed sector determined by classified LST blocks and gauge anomaly data from the remaining gauge-neutral E-string sector, and a BPS refinement of the Completeness Conjecture that ensures population of the relevant charge rays. We further show that this reconstruction provides new constraints on the low-energy theory and can rule out candidate EFTs that pass all previously known local lattice and anomaly consistency conditions. Separately, for theories admitting geometric tensor bases, we explain how the same reconstruction determines the complete Mori cone of the corresponding K\"ahler surface.
papers.summary: The authors develop an effective‑field‑theory based algorithm to reconstruct the full cone of BPS string charges in 6d (1,0) supergravity, using the universal H‑string and anomaly data to isolate primitive generators and impose a refined completeness conjecture. This method yields new consistency constraints on candidate EFTs and, for geometrically realizable models, recovers the Mori cone of the associated Kähler surface.

papers.title: All-multiplicity completion of maximally supersymmetric gauge amplitudes
papers.authors: Ilmo Sung
papers.abstract: We show that the known six-point constraints on four-point amplitudes are sufficient for completion at arbitrary multiplicity in planar, four-dimensional maximally supersymmetric gauge theory. We construct massless tree amplitudes as formal series in the derivative expansion, with the standard supersymmetric Yang-Mills three-point amplitudes, unbroken R-symmetry, and parity invariance of amplitudes with only external scalars, holding the scalar labels fixed. For a positive leading four-point contact coefficient, the even coefficients in the logarithmic parameterization are fixed, while every real sequence of odd coefficients is realized by a completion at all derivative orders. The construction uses the field-theory Kawai-Lewellen-Tye bilinear and normalized matrices of sphere integrals. Exponentiating homogeneous components of their matrix logarithms varies the odd coefficients independently while preserving locality and factorization through the complete massless multiplet. The six-point conditions are therefore necessary and sufficient for such a completion. Higher-multiplicity consistency imposes no further restrictions on these four-point coefficients once the higher-point contact interactions are chosen consistently with the same symmetries and factorization conditions.
papers.summary: The authors show that the six‑point constraints on four‑point amplitudes in planar μ=4 SYM uniquely fix the entire derivative expansion for any multiplicity, using KLT bilinears and sphere integrals to build local, factorizing tree amplitudes. This establishes that no further higher‑point consistency conditions are required once the contact interactions respect supersymmetry, R‑symmetry, and parity.

papers.title: Generalised Gibbs Ensembles from the ODE/IM Correspondence: the Lee--Yang Model
papers.authors: Sujay K. Ashok, Max Downing, Faisal Karimi, Adarsh Sudhakar, Roberto Tateo
papers.abstract: We introduce a systematic scheme for constructing the ODE/IM counterpart of generalised Gibbs ensembles, and apply it to the chiral sector of the Lee--Yang conformal field theory. We encode the chemical potentials in a deformation of the cubic oscillator, fixed order by order by requiring that the large-energy WKB period reproduces exactly the driving term of the corresponding thermodynamic Bethe ansatz equation; the subleading WKB periods then yield, as predictions, the deformed eigenvalues of the local conserved charges. We work out the spin-5 ensemble in detail for two states of the model: the ground state, in the module of the primary $\phi$, dual to the deformed cubic oscillator, and the primary of the identity module, dual to the same oscillator supplemented by an apparent singularity, a double pole whose position is fixed by a trivial-monodromy condition. In both cases, the Stokes multiplier obeys the Lee--Yang Y-system, and the deformed eigenvalues match, to the orders checked, an independent conformal-field-theory computation. The Borel resummation of the resulting series for the ground-state energy reproduces the numerical TBA solution over many orders of magnitude in the chemical potential. The scheme relies only on general features of the ODE/IM correspondence and applies to generalised Gibbs ensembles in other integrable models.
papers.summary: This work develops a systematic method to construct generalized Gibbs ensembles via the ODE/IM correspondence, applying it to the Lee–Yang conformal field theory. By deforming a cubic oscillator and matching WKB periods to the TBA driving terms, the authors compute deformed eigenvalues of local charges and confirm them against CFT calculations, demonstrating the method’s effectiveness across integrable models.

papers.title: Carroll-Weyl gauged null strings in AdS
papers.authors: Sarthak Duary, Sourav Maji
papers.abstract: We study the Carroll-Weyl gauged null string in the Poincar\'e patch of $\mathrm{AdS}_D$ and its BRST quantization. In Poincar\'e coordinates $X^A=(z,x^i)$, the radial conformal Killing vector $K=\partial_z$ becomes homothetic in a suitable conformally related frame. A field-dependent rescaling of the homothetic Hamiltonian constraint then leads to the radial-adapted basis $\mathcal{M}=\frac{1}{2}(P_z^2+P_iP^i)$, $\mathcal{L}=-P_AX'^A$, and $\mathcal{S}=P_z$, with $\mathcal{M}$ invariant along the Carroll-Weyl radial flow. Their modes form a $\mathrm{BMS}_3$ algebra extended by an abelian weight-one current. We classify the central extensions allowed by this residual algebra and find four independent cohomology classes in the $LL$, $LM$, $LS$, and $SS$ channels. We then construct the associated BRST complex, including the ghost pair for the radial Carroll-Weyl constraint. In the canonical highest-weight first-order representation, only the Virasoro-type central extension is realized: $(c_{LL},c_{LM},c_{LS},c_{SS})=(2D-54,0,0,0)$. Cancellation of the corresponding nontrivial BRST cocycle therefore gives $D=27$ in this representation. This differs structurally from the minimal flat Carroll-Weyl theory, where the dilation constraint $X\cdot P$ gives extra anomaly channels.
papers.summary: This work studies a Carroll‑Weyl gauged null string in AdS, deriving a radial‑adapted BMS$_3$ algebra with a weight‑one current and classifying its central extensions. The BRST analysis forces the critical dimension to $D=27$ in the highest‑weight representation, revealing a novel anomaly structure distinct from flat‑space null strings.

papers.title: Surface defects in $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super Yang-Mills: exact results and holographic bootstrap
papers.authors: Lorenzo Bianchi, Davide Bonomi, Maddalena Ferragatta, Valentina Forini
papers.abstract: We study two-point functions of chiral primary operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super Yang-Mills in the presence of a half-BPS surface defect. Such a defect preserves only the diagonal combination of transverse rotations and of a global U(1) R-symmetry, so that the correlator depends on one additional cross-ratio and splits into sectors of definite angular charge. We solve the superconformal Ward identities and construct the bulk and defect superconformal blocks in all sectors, including the charged ones, which have no analogue for defects preserving transverse rotations. The solution contains a holomorphic sector, which we fix non-perturbatively by mapping it to a chiral algebra correlator. We extend this map to defects breaking transverse rotations, where it requires a redefinition of the modes of the two-dimensional current algebra, and use it to fix the charged sectors as well. We then use the defect dispersion relation to reconstruct the full correlator of the dimension-two chiral primary at leading order at large N and strong coupling. In the charged sectors long multiplets are absent and the answer is conjecturally exact in both N and the coupling; expanding it at weak coupling, we find perfect agreement with known results. From these correlators we extract infinitely many new pieces of defect CFT data. Finally, we reproduce the strong-coupling answer by an independent Witten diagram bootstrap on the rotation-invariant locus.
papers.summary: The authors compute two-point functions of chiral primaries in $mathcal{N}=4$ SYM with a half-BPS surface defect, solving superconformal Ward identities and constructing bulk and defect superconformal blocks, including charged sectors that lack transverse rotation symmetry. Using a chiral algebra map and a defect dispersion relation they obtain exact large‑$N$ strong‑coupling results, confirm weak‑coupling expansions, and reproduce the correlator via a Witten‑diagram bootstrap on the rotation‑invariant locus.

papers.title: The hidden sunrise in the energy-energy correlator
papers.authors: Matthew D. Schwartz, Xiaoyuan Zhang
papers.abstract: The energy-energy correlator (EEC) is one of a handful of collider observables that can be computed analytically to high orders. As an energy-weighted cross-section, it exposes features of quantum field theory that scattering amplitudes do not, and it can be compared directly to data. As with scattering amplitudes, the analytic expressions require special functions beyond polylogarithms. In Henn et al., the EEC was computed to next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) for $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills (SYM) theory, and the result is expressed in terms of both harmonic polylogarithms (HPLs) and one two-fold integral, which contains elliptic curves. In this work, we report a complete result including the remaining elliptic sector, which is closely related to the sunrise Feynman integrals. We find the $j$-invariants of the EEC and the sunrise agree identically under a M\"obius map, and thus the elliptic sector in the EEC lives on the $\Gamma_1(6)$ modular curve of the sunrise integral. We then express the answer in terms of iterated Eisenstein integrals, which can be evaluated to high precision quickly. The analytic form also allows a first study of the EEC Landau bootstrap, and the understanding of its function space in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM offers a concrete handle on the elliptic sector of the EEC in QCD. Many of the technical results in this paper were completed with AI under human supervision.
papers.summary: This paper completes the NNLO computation of the energy-energy correlator in N=4 SYM, including the previously missing elliptic sector tied to the sunrise integral. The authors show that the elliptic structure lives on the Γ1(6) modular curve and express the result in terms of iterated Eisenstein integrals, enabling high-precision evaluation and opening a new avenue for studying the EEC’s Landau singularities.

papers.title: Polynomial and Eigenspace Factorisations for the One-loop Dilatation Operator at Finite $N$
papers.authors: Adrian Padellaro, Sanjaye Ramgoolam, Ryo Suzuki
papers.abstract: We study gauge-invariant two-matrix polynomials of degree $L$, corresponding to the states in the $su(2)$ sector of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory with gauge group $U(N)$ or $SU(N)$ at finite $N$. For the $U(N)$ theory, the state space has the structure of an algebra $\mathcal{A}_N(L)$, which is a direct sum of permutation centraliser algebras, i.e. sub-algebras of the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[S_L]$ of $S_L$. For $N \ge L$, $\mathcal{A}_N (L) = \mathcal{A} (L)$ is independent of $N$, and the one-loop dilatation operator acts on $\mathcal{A}(L)$ with $N$ as a parameter. For $N < L$, $\mathcal{A}_N (L)$ is a subspace of $\mathcal{A}(L)$ defined using a finite-$N$ cutoff on Young diagrams with $L$ boxes. We establish two results on the eigenspaces of the one-loop dilatation operator. Our first main result is that the characteristic polynomial of the one-loop dilatation operator on $\mathcal{A}_N(L)$ divides the characteristic polynomial from $\mathcal{A}(L)$, continued to $N < L$. Our second result is that each eigenstate of the one-loop dilatation operator in the $SU(N)$ theory generates an infinite tower of eigenstates in the $U(N)$ theory, through the multiplication of single-letter traces. These towers define an eigenspace factorisation of the $U(N)$ theory labelled by the number of such traces. Further, we conjecture that the space of $SU(N)$-invariant polynomials in two traceless matrices at finite $N$ is isomorphic to the intersection of $\mathcal{A}_N(L)$ with the subspace of $\mathbb{C}[S_L]$ spanned by derangements. This intersection conjecture is supported by dimension counting. Finally, we propose a one-loop dilatation operator on the intersection, thus providing a direct permutation framework for the $SU(N)$ spectral problem at finite $N$. The computed spectra based on the proposal agree with the prediction from the eigenspace factorisation in the $U(N)$ theory.
papers.summary: The paper develops a permutation‑algebraic framework for the one‑loop dilatation operator in the su(2) sector of finite‑N N=4 SYM, showing how its eigenspaces factorise into towers of U(N) states generated by single‑letter traces and proving that the characteristic polynomial for finite N divides the infinite‑N one. It further conjectures an isomorphism between SU(N) gauge‑invariant polynomials and a derangement subspace, providing a direct permutation‑based spectral problem that matches explicit one‑loop spectra.

papers.title: Fourier analysis of compact oscillons
papers.authors: Pawel Klimas, Leandro Roza Livramento, Jo\~ao Saldanha Streibel
papers.abstract: We present a new derivation of the exact compact oscillon in the signum-Gordon model using Fourier methods. This approach decomposes the oscillon into an infinite, uniformly convergent series of discrete modes consisting of a fundamental frequency and its odd higher harmonics, in contrast to standard analytic potentials, where the corresponding infinite perturbative series fails to converge. Crucially, our oscillon evades the non-existence theorem for spatially localized, small-amplitude periodic states. We investigate the accuracy of truncating the Fourier series and find that the primary mode alone provides a remarkably accurate approximation of the exact solution, with agreement improving significantly when the first two non-vanishing harmonic modes are included. Furthermore, we generalize this framework to a swaying compact oscillon with a periodically moving boundary. We show that describing such an oscillon requires even-order modes, whose coupling with the odd source terms induces a dynamic modulation that generates the swaying motion, even though the spatial Fourier profiles themselves are time-independent.
papers.summary: This paper derives an exact compact oscillon solution in the signum-Gordon model via Fourier decomposition, showing that the fundamental mode alone gives a good approximation and that higher odd harmonics improve accuracy. It also extends the method to a swaying oscillon with a moving boundary, revealing that even-order modes couple to odd source terms to produce dynamic modulation.

papers.title: Reconstruction of Black Hole Islands from Hawking Radiation via the Algebraic Petz Map
papers.authors: Niloofar Vardian
papers.abstract: The island proposal guarantees a unitary Page curve for evaporating black holes, implying that operators deep behind the horizon must be fully reconstructable from asymptotic Hawking radiation. However, because the interior is causally disconnected and highly dynamical, standard entanglement wedge reconstruction methods, relying on global isometries or continuous modular flow, fail to provide this mapping. We resolve this by constructing a protocol for island reconstruction using the algebraic Petz map. By using modular theory, we reflect island operators into the accessible complement, transport them to the boundary, and map them into the radiation algebra. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this purely algebraic derivation naturally yields the structure of Papadodimas-Raju mirror operators. This framework provides a rigorous operational dictionary for the island formula, proving that information trapped inside a black hole can be decoded.
papers.summary: The paper presents a rigorous algebraic construction of the Petz map to reconstruct interior operators of an evaporating black hole from Hawking radiation, thereby providing a concrete realization of the island formula. It shows that modular theory can be used to map island degrees of freedom to the radiation algebra, reproducing the structure of Papadodimas–Raju mirror operators.

papers.title: Beyond gauge-parameter dependence: Further evidence for asymptotic safety in Scalar-Tensor theories
papers.authors: Samuel M. P. Antunes, Antonio D. Pereira
papers.abstract: Asymptotic Safety provides a promising framework for the quantization of Scalar-Tensor theories as non-perturbatively renormalizable quantum field theories. Over the past years, growing evidence has accumulated for the existence of non-trivial renormalization group fixed points in a variety of Scalar-Tensor models. In this work, we investigate the robustness of these fixed points under significant modifications of the computational setup. In particular, we employ a gauge condition that explicitly depends on the dynamical scalar field, going beyond a mere gauge-parameter deformation of the standard linear covariant gauges commonly used in the literature. Exploring different field parameterizations, we identify fixed points belonging to the Gaussian Matter class in four spacetime dimensions that are consistent with previous studies. The real part of the critical exponents associated with the scalar-field mass and the non-minimal scalar-curvature coupling turn out to have very small absolute value. We provide a comprehensive exploration of how the anomalous dimension of the scalar field and field parameterization impact those critical exponents showing that fixed-point candidates with two or four relevant directions emerge.
papers.summary: This paper investigates the robustness of non‑trivial RG fixed points in scalar‑tensor theories by introducing a scalar‑field‑dependent gauge condition and exploring different field parameterizations. The authors find Gaussian Matter class fixed points with small critical exponents and show that the number of relevant directions can vary between two and four depending on the anomalous dimension and parameterization.

papers.title: The three- and four-loop equal-mass sunset integrals and local Calabi--Yau fourfolds and fivefolds
papers.authors: Hartmut Maennel, Pierre Vanhove
papers.abstract: We determine the equal-mass two-dimensional three- and four-loop sunset Feynman integrals $I^{(3)}_\circleddash$ and $I^{(4)}_\circleddash$ at large Euclidean momentum in terms of the genus-zero Gromov--Witten theory of the local Calabi--Yau fourfold and fivefold $X_L=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_L})$, where $F_L\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{L+1}$, $L=3,4$, is a smooth hypersurface of multidegree $(1,\ldots,1)$. At two loops the sunset integral is governed by the prepotential of a local Calabi--Yau threefold. For $L\geq3$ the moduli spaces of unmarked stable maps have positive virtual dimension and there is no prepotential, therefore the Feynman integral is governed instead by the one-point potential $\mathcal F_{\gamma_L}$ with insertion $\gamma_L=H^{L-1}/(L-1)!$, by its gravitational descendants, and by $\zeta(3)$ boundary terms coming from the Gamma class. At both loop orders the coefficient of $R^{L-1}$ in the Frobenius expansion in the mirror coordinate $R$ is $-\theta_Q\mathcal F_{\gamma_L}$ with the Novikov variable $Q=\exp(R)$. At three loops the whole Feynman integral is an explicit expression in $\mathcal F_{\gamma_3}$ alone, because genus-zero recursion determines all descendant series from it; at four loops two diagonal series suffice, and the $\zeta(3)$ term is itself corrected by $\theta_Q\mathcal F_{\gamma_4}$. At three loops we also derive the analytic normalization independently, from the Picard--Fuchs equation and the polar part of a Mellin transform, prove integrality of the multiple-cover transforms for arbitrary integral insertions together with an explicit quantum-$K$ formula, and compute the exact period connection polynomials. Finally we give endpoint values along the Euclidean axis, bounds on the Taylor radii in the Novikov variable $Q$, a computer-assisted proof of the four-loop endpoint nonanalyticity, and a comparison of the normalizations at two, three and four loops.
papers.summary: This paper evaluates two-dimensional three- and four-loop sunset integrals using genus‑zero Gromov–Witten theory of local Calabi–Yau fourfolds and fivefolds, linking the integrals to one‑point potentials and gravitational descendants. It also derives analytic normalizations, integrality of multiple‑cover transforms, and endpoint behavior, but does not directly address holography, celestial amplitudes, or related topics.

papers.title: Massive de Sitter Correlators as Finite Mellin-Barnes Integrals
papers.authors: Amara McCune
papers.abstract: Using the Mellin-Barnes representation of de Sitter propagators, we reduce tree-level heavy-particle exchange to finite integrals that converge at physical kinematics on mass-independent contours, and one-loop diagrams to the same integrand times a flat-space momentum factor. We evaluate the triple-exchange bispectrum without analytic continuation and compute the complete one-loop triangle at general mass. These give cosmological collider predictions, the oscillatory signatures of heavy particles during inflation, for multiple exchanges and loops at arbitrary masses.
papers.summary: This paper develops a finite Mellin-Barnes representation for tree-level and one-loop de Sitter correlators, enabling direct evaluation of heavy-particle exchange without analytic continuation. The authors compute the bispectrum from triple exchange and the full one-loop triangle for arbitrary masses, providing explicit cosmological collider signatures for multiple exchanges and loops.

papers.title: Quantum geometry at arbitrary genus - I: Anharmonic potentials
papers.authors: Mustafa T\"ure, Mithat \"Unsal
papers.abstract: In quantum mechanics of genus-1 potentials, perturbation theory around the topologically trivial saddle and non-perturbative instanton saddle are constructively related via the P/NP relation. Whether such a relation persists for higher-genus potentials has remained an open problem. In this work, we resolve it using tools from complex algebraic geometry combined with exact WKB. The classical energy conservation relation $p^2 = 2(E-V(q))$ defines a genus-g Riemann surface $X$, whose periods are naturally organized by its Jacobian variety $J(X) = \mathbb{C}^{\text{g}}/\Lambda$ via the Abel-Jacobi map, and independently by the solution basis of the associated Picard-Fuchs equations. We show that the physically relevant, WKB-active cycles are generally related to the Picard-Fuchs basis by a linear transformation that lies in $\text{SL}(2\text{g},\mathbb{Z})$ but not in the symplectic group $\text{Sp}(2\text{g},\mathbb{Z})$ once $\text{g}\geq2$, in contrast to the genus-1 case, where the two groups coincide. This mismatch is the obstruction that has made an explicit higher-genus P/NP relation elusive. We show that it can be resolved by passing to a modified Riemann bilinear identity, built from a suitably transformed intersection matrix, which the WKB-active periods do satisfy exactly. The result is an all-orders quantum P/NP relation valid for potentials of arbitrary genus, which we derive explicitly for genus-2 (quintic and sextic) and genus-3 (septic and octic) anharmonic oscillators.
papers.summary: This paper extends the perturbative/non‑perturbative (P/NP) relation known for genus‑1 anharmonic oscillators to arbitrary genus by exploiting the geometry of the associated Riemann surface and Picard‑Fuchs equations. Using a modified Riemann bilinear identity, the authors derive an exact all‑orders P/NP relation for genus‑2 and genus‑3 anharmonic potentials, resolving a long‑standing obstruction that arises when the WKB‑active cycles lie outside the symplectic group.

papers.title: Fermionic Spectral Functions in a Two-Current Gubser-Rocha Model with Axion Momentum Relaxation
papers.authors: Cai-E Liu, Defu Hou
papers.abstract: We investigate fermionic spectral functions in a two-current Gubser-Rocha background with linear-axion momentum relaxation. Serving as a comparison channel, the dipole coupling $p_1$ is found to produce a soft asymmetric reconstruction without opening a clean hard Mott gap. Our main analysis then focuses on two axion-dependent non-minimal couplings modulated by current mixing. The $p_2$ tensor channel suppresses the zero-energy Fermi peak and shifts the dominant spectral weight to finite frequencies, resulting in a flat-bottom reconstruction. In contrast, the $p_3$ vector channel creates a strong spectral asymmetry in momentum space, generating open, Fermi-arc-like segments. Varying the momentum-relaxation strength $\beta/\mu$ and the doping parameter $\chi$ reveals a channel-dependent response to the two-current background. Increasing $\beta/\mu$ generally broadens the $p_2$ response, whereas the one-sided $p_3$ feature varies non-monotonically under changes of the background parameters. These results clarify how current mixing, axion-induced momentum relaxation, and non-minimal fermion couplings jointly reshape holographic fermionic excitations. These results clarify how current mixing, axion-induced momentum relaxation, and non-minimal fermion couplings jointly reshape holographic fermionic excitations.
papers.summary: This paper studies fermionic spectral functions in a two-current Gubser-Rocha holographic model with linear axion momentum relaxation, focusing on how dipole and non-minimal couplings modify the spectral weight and produce features such as flat-bottom reconstructions and Fermi-arc-like segments. The analysis shows that axion-induced momentum relaxation and current mixing significantly reshape the holographic fermionic excitations, providing insights into strongly coupled systems.

papers.title: Quantum Gravity in Asymptotically Flat Spacetimes from Unstable D-Branes
papers.authors: Roji Pius
papers.abstract: We present a non-perturbative formulation of quantum gravity in asymptotically flat spacetimes using Witten's cubic open string field theory (OSFT) on unstable D-branes. Given that the massless spin-2 sector of the closed string spectrum inherently encodes the degrees of freedom of quantum gravity, we establish this connection by mapping on-shell closed string excitations directly to gauge-invariant operators in OSFT, realizing a concrete flat-space analogue of the AdS/CFT correspondence. By evaluating the OSFT correlation functions of these operators perturbatively around the tachyon vacuum, we systematically reproduce the all-orders genus expansion of the closed string S-matrix for the associated states. This demonstrates that closed string theory-and thus quantum gravity-emerges dynamically from the open string tachyon vacuum, establishing Witten's OSFT as a fully calculable, non-perturbative framework for flat-space quantum gravity.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a non‑perturbative description of quantum gravity in asymptotically flat spacetimes by using Witten’s cubic open string field theory on unstable D‑branes. By mapping on‑shell closed‑string excitations to gauge‑invariant OSFT operators, the authors recover the full closed‑string S‑matrix perturbatively around the tachyon vacuum, realizing a flat‑space analogue of holography.

papers.title: No Particle Production and Integrability in AdS$_2$
papers.authors: De-liang Zhong, Xinan Zhou
papers.abstract: We propose an analogue of the no particle production condition in two-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, and demonstrate how this criterion uniquely reconstructs the curved-space Liouville and Toda theories via general-multiplicity holographic correlators.
papers.summary: The authors formulate a no‑particle‑production condition for quantum fields in AdS$_2$ and show that it uniquely fixes the dynamics of the curved‑space Liouville and Toda models. By computing general‑multiplicity holographic correlators they demonstrate that integrability emerges from this constraint, providing a new bridge between AdS/CFT and 2D integrable field theories.

papers.title: Dielectric constant of holographic insulator from quantum geometry
papers.authors: Debabrata Ghorai, Taewon Yuk, Sang-Jin Sin
papers.abstract: We study dielectric properties of holographic insulators from the quantum geometry of the ground state. We realize the insulating state by the pseudoscalar interaction of holographic fermions and calculate the fermionic Green function to extract the effective hamiltonian. We then derive the quantum metric and Berry curvature to compute the transports and finally get the dielectric constant from the imaginary part of conductivity.
papers.summary: The paper investigates the dielectric response of a holographic insulator by computing the fermionic Green function and extracting the effective Hamiltonian, then using the quantum metric and Berry curvature to evaluate transport coefficients. It ultimately obtains the dielectric constant from the imaginary part of the conductivity, linking quantum geometry to macroscopic dielectric properties.

papers.title: Extremal black hole mimickers: geometry, stability, and long-delay signal trains
papers.authors: Sergey N. Solodukhin
papers.abstract: We present a spacetime that serves as a horizonless mimicker of extremal black holes. Unlike previously studied mimickers of black holes with non-degenerate horizons, whose geometries are of the wormhole type and consist of two asymptotically flat regions connected by a very long throat, the mimicker of an extremal black hole possesses a single asymptotically flat region at one end and an infinitely long throat at the other. In the throat region, the spacetime approaches the direct-product geometry $M_{1,1} \times S^2$, where $M_{1,1}$ is two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime and $S^2$ is the two-sphere. We investigate scalar-field dynamics and the fate of the Aretakis instability. Although Aretakis-like modes arise in a local analysis of the throat, they do not lead to a physical instability of the mimicker. A scalar perturbation initially localized in the throat gives rise, at late times, to a sequence of signals with a characteristic separation $t_{\rm delay}\sim 1/\lambda$, where $\lambda\ll 1$ is a deformation parameter. This timescale is parametrically larger than the echo time $t_{\rm echo}\sim \ln(1/\lambda)$ characteristic of non-extremal black-hole mimickers. We refer to this sequence as a {\it long-delay signal train}. Geometrically, the periodicity of the long-delay signals is associated with periodic geodesics on $S^2$. We then extend the construction to extremal Kerr. In this case, the throat region approaches a generalized product geometry involving $M_{1,1}$ and a two-dimensional surface $\Sigma_2$. The corresponding signals are expected to form a quasi-periodic signal train, reflecting the quasi-periodic geodesic motion on $\Sigma_2$. We also comment on the generalization to wormhole mimickers of non-extremal black holes and on the implications of these results for unitarity in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a horizonless spacetime that mimics an extremal black hole, featuring an infinitely long throat approaching a product of 2D Minkowski space and a sphere, and studies scalar perturbations revealing a long‑delay train of echoes tied to geodesics on the sphere. The analysis shows that Aretakis‑type instabilities are absent, and the results have implications for unitarity in AdS/CFT and the structure of echoes in extremal versus non‑extremal mimickers.

papers.title: Entanglement entropy of black holes from the first law of thermodynamics
papers.authors: D. V. Diakonov, Gleb S. Zverev
papers.abstract: We compute the entanglement entropy of quantum matter in spacetimes with a Killing horizon entirely on-shell, by integrating the first law of thermodynamics along a one-parameter family of equilibrium backgrounds labelled by the Hawking temperature. This yields a closed expression in terms of the renormalized stress-energy tensor and the Killing vector, finite by construction, with no replicas and no conical singularities. Its covariant form agrees with the matter terms of the Bardeen--Carter--Hawking mass variation formula. We show in details that for static patch of de Sitter space and for the non-rotating BTZ black hole it reproduces the conical entropy exactly, contact term $Q$ included.
papers.summary: The paper derives a closed-form, replica‑free expression for the entanglement entropy of quantum fields in spacetimes with a Killing horizon by integrating the first law of thermodynamics along a one‑parameter family of equilibrium backgrounds, yielding a finite result expressed in terms of the renormalized stress‑energy tensor and the Killing vector. It verifies that for the static patch of de Sitter space and the non‑rotating BTZ black hole this expression reproduces the conical entropy—including the contact term Q—and matches the matter terms of the Bardeen–Carter–Hawking mass variation formula.

papers.title: Einstein-Cartan and Palatini-Cartan Gravity from Graded Poisson Geometry
papers.authors: Johannes Moerland, Peter Schupp
papers.abstract: Using notions from graded Poisson geometry, we develop a framework that allows for concise formulations of field theories such as Einstein-Cartan and Palatini-Cartan gravity. We show that Einstein-Cartan gravity is equivalent to a variant of Palatini-Cartan gravity in which the vielbein fields are constrained to satisfy appropriate symmetry relations, which we refer to as constrained vielbein gravity. To that end, we relate these theories via a diffeomorphism of graded manifolds. We then show how to obtain the full Palatini-Cartan theory by removing the symmetry constraint. Finally, we show how our graded geometric framework allows for a direct incorporation of the minimal BV extension of the graded constrained vielbein and Palatini-Cartan theories.
papers.summary: The authors use graded Poisson geometry to recast Einstein‑Cartan and Palatini‑Cartan gravity, showing their equivalence via a symmetry constraint on the vielbein. They further extend the framework to include the minimal BV formalism for these theories.

papers.title: Multipartite Entanglement Geometry in AdS/BCFT
papers.authors: Debarshi Basu, Qiang Wen, Mingshuai Xu
papers.abstract: Multipartite entanglement measures probe how quantum correlations are organized beyond what can be inferred from pairwise entropies. We study how this structure is reshaped by a physical boundary in a holographic BCFT. The end-of-the-world brane opens new relative-homology channels for multipartite entanglement, allowing connected bulk webs to reorganize and factorize at scales that need not coincide with any ordinary Ryu--Takayanagi transition. In static AdS$_3$/BCFT$_2$, this produces a characteristic hierarchy of multipartite phases and a nontrivial dependence of genuine multi-entropy on the boundary. In the thermofield-double state, genuinely connected webs can instead be supported through the Einstein--Rosen bridge, leading to growth, reconnection and saturation scales distinct from the usual Hartman--Maldacena transitions. These results show that multipartite entanglement is sensitive not only to extremal-surface areas but also to how bulk entanglement structures are allowed to join, split and terminate in the presence of a boundary.
papers.summary: This paper investigates how multipartite entanglement structures reorganize in holographic BCFTs due to the presence of an end‑of‑the‑world brane, revealing new relative‑homology channels that allow bulk entanglement webs to factorize at scales distinct from standard RT transitions. The study extends to thermofield‑double states, showing that Einstein–Rosen bridges can support genuinely connected webs, leading to novel growth, reconnection, and saturation scales beyond Hartman–Maldacena dynamics.

papers.title: Mass quench in interacting finite-size quantum field system
papers.authors: Grachik A Simonian, Alexey G. Mikhaylenko, Andrew G. Semenov
papers.abstract: In this work, we theoretically investigate the non-equilibrium evolution of the correlation functions of a quantum scalar field following a mass quantum quench in a finite-size system. The self-consistent equation for the Keldysh (statistical) correlation function is solved numerically in the one-loop approximation. A specific spatio-temporal effect is observed: at a point in time approximately equal to half the system size, the effective mass experiences a strong disturbance. It is shown that this effect is driven by the interference of counter-propagating wave fronts of fluctuations that propagate within the light cone and is induced by periodic boundary conditions.
papers.summary: This paper studies the non‑equilibrium dynamics of a scalar field after a mass quench in a finite‑size system, solving the Keldysh correlation function at one‑loop order. It finds a pronounced disturbance in the effective mass at half the system size, attributed to interference of counter‑propagating fluctuations under periodic boundary conditions.

papers.title: Probability measures for de Sitter JT gravity
papers.authors: Wilfried Buchmuller, Alexander Westphal
papers.abstract: Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity with positive cosmological constant is a toy model to study the emergence of expanding de Sitter universes from a quantum state. Its density matrix is a superposition of double-trumpet amplitudes which are solutions of a Wheeler-DeWitt equation. We compare predictions of such mixed states for classical expanding universes with the corresponding predictions of no-boundary wavefunctions. Double-trumpet amplitudes consistent with holography, whose semiclassical limit matches the result from Schwarzian boundary fluctuations, lead to a flat probability distribution for the size of the universe, consistent with models of inflation. This is in contrast to the suppression of large universes predicted by no-boundary wave functions.
papers.summary: This work studies JT gravity with a positive cosmological constant, formulating its density matrix as a superposition of double‑trumpet amplitudes that solve the Wheeler–DeWitt equation. By comparing these mixed states to no‑boundary wavefunctions, the authors find that holographically consistent double‑trumpet solutions yield a flat probability distribution for the size of a de Sitter universe, in contrast to the suppression of large universes predicted by the no‑boundary proposal.

papers.title: Asymptotic Safety in Gauge Theories beyond Four Dimensions: Perturbative Tests and Fixed-Point Mergers
papers.authors: Aldo Deandrea, Jie Liu, Roman Pasechnik, Zhi-Wei Wang, Yu-Bo Zhao
papers.abstract: Non-Abelian gauge theories above four dimensions may admit an interacting ultraviolet fixed point through the competition between canonical scaling and gauge-field antiscreening. Using the four-loop $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ beta function continued to $D=4+2\epsilon$, we determine the largest dimension $D_{\mathrm{pt}}=4+2\epsilon_{\mathrm{pt}}$ below which successive loop corrections to the fixed point remain hierarchically ordered under a specified ratio criterion, and map $D_{\mathrm{pt}}$ over color and flavor numbers for fermions in the fundamental representation of $SU(N)$. At $D=5$, we construct rational anomalous dimensions with a fixed, pole-regularized denominator inspired by the functional renormalization group (fRG). Matching to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ series through one, two, and three loops produces progressively smaller shifts in the critical flavor number and coupling at the ultraviolet--infrared merger (the point where the infrared and ultraviolet fixed points coincide), yielding $N_f^{\mathrm{cr}}\simeq 2.09 \, N$ at large $N$ in the three-loop construction. This low-order stabilization, together with qualitative evidence from fRG flows including higher gauge operators, suggests a potential merger scenario that bounds the candidate asymptotically safe region in flavor number. The resulting color--flavor map provides guidance for five-dimensional model building by displaying both the baseline perturbative-control boundary and the candidate three-loop merger boundary. Four-loop matching, however, retains an interacting ultraviolet fixed point beyond the three-loop merger boundary, with no merger found for integer $2\le N\le15$ and $0\le N_f/N\le11/2$. The sensitivity of the fixed-point structure to higher-order terms leaves both scenarios open, highlighting fixed-point annihilation as a potential constraint on five-dimensional asymptotic safety.
papers.summary: The authors extend the four‑loop MS‑bar beta function to D=4+2ε and identify the largest dimension where perturbative control of an interacting UV fixed point persists, then construct rational approximants to anomalous dimensions at D=5 that suggest a UV–IR fixed‑point merger delimiting a candidate asymptotically safe region in the color–flavor plane, while higher‑order terms keep the scenario inconclusive.

papers.title: Horizon symmetries of exact hydrodynamic actions
papers.authors: Mike Blake, Arpit Das, Richard A. Davison
papers.abstract: We demonstrate how horizon symmetries of AdS black holes are realised in the hydrodynamic actions for the dynamics of the dual stress tensor. A recent approach for obtaining such actions involves a choice of horizon boundary conditions, and we show that diffeomorphisms that preserve these give rise to symmetries of the corresponding hydrodynamic action. We obtain explicit hydrodynamic actions for small amplitude perturbations of black holes in JT and AdS$_3$ gravity using this approach and demonstrate explicitly the existence of these symmetries. For a natural choice of boundary conditions, the resulting actions manifestly realise gauge symmetries previously proposed for effective theories of maximal chaos.
papers.summary: The paper shows how diffeomorphisms preserving horizon boundary conditions generate symmetries of hydrodynamic actions for dual stress tensors of AdS black holes, and constructs explicit actions for JT and AdS3 perturbations. It demonstrates that these actions realize gauge symmetries linked to maximal chaos, providing a concrete link between horizon symmetries and effective hydrodynamic descriptions.

papers.title: Stringy resolution of bouncing singularities
papers.authors: Ilija Buri\'c, Ivan Gusev, Andrei Parnachev
papers.abstract: We study the near-horizon geometry of near-extremal NS5 branes, which admits an exact worldsheet description in terms of the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})_k/U(1)$ coset. In the supergravity limit, the analytically continued time-domain reflection amplitude exhibits a singularity associated with a null geodesic bouncing off the black-hole singularity, analogous to the bouncing singularities of boundary correlators in asymptotically AdS spacetimes. We show that finite-string-length effects render this amplitude an entire function of complex time, completely resolving the bouncing singularity. This resolution is nonperturbative in the inverse coset level: the singularity persists at every finite order in the expansion.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes the near‑horizon geometry of near‑extremal NS5 branes using the exact SL(2,ℝ)_k/U(1) coset CFT and finds that the time‑domain reflection amplitude, which exhibits a bouncing singularity in the supergravity limit, becomes an entire function once finite string‑length effects are included. This non‑perturbative resolution of the singularity persists at every finite order in the 1/k expansion, providing a stringy smoothing of the null‑geodesic bounce analogous to boundary correlator singularities in AdS/CFT.

papers.title: Cornering the Heterotic String
papers.authors: Li-Yuan Chiang, Yu-tin Huang, He-Chen Weng
papers.abstract: We study tree-level completions of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ Yang--Mills theory coupled to $\mathcal N=4$ supergravity. Six-point factorization and supersymmetry Ward identities, supplemented by a peculiar-parity restriction on scalar contact terms, impose nonlinear relations between the single- and double-trace Wilson coefficients, $a_{k,q}$ and $b_{k,q}$, of the four-gluon amplitude. The simplest relation, $\kappa^2a_{0,0}=0$, excludes the single-trace $F^4$ interaction at nonzero gravitational coupling, despite its compatibility with four-point supersymmetry. On this gravitational branch, five double-trace parameters determine all coefficients through $a_{7,q}$ and $b_{8,q}$, which are reproduced by a common exponential generating form. Both the heterotic string and a family of infinite-spin-tower (IST) amplitudes realize this structure. Combining these relations with dispersion relations and partial-wave positivity in $SO(N)$ color channels yields a narrow numerical band closely bounded by the heterotic and simplest IST amplitudes. A spin-dependent mass gap excludes the IST spectrum and further localizes the region near the heterotic trajectory. An analytic unitarity analysis of the simplest IST gives $N\leq48$ and $g^2/(\kappa^2 m^2)\leq4$, matching the upper limits of the heterotic amplitude, where $m$ is the mass of the first massive level. Along the heterotic trajectory, the numerical bounds also sharply constrain the gauge-to-gravity coupling ratio at $N=48$.
papers.summary: The paper derives nonlinear constraints on the Wilson coefficients of four-gluon amplitudes in $mathcal N=4$ SYM coupled to supergravity, showing that the heterotic string and a family of infinite-spin-tower amplitudes saturate these bounds. By combining supersymmetry, factorization, and partial-wave positivity, the authors narrow the allowed parameter space and obtain quantitative limits on the gauge-to-gravity coupling and the spectrum of massive states.

papers.title: Differential $T_2$-Duality and Spans of Principal 3-Bundles with Connections
papers.authors: Gianni Gagliardo, Christian Saemann, Roberto Tellez-Dominguez
papers.abstract: We present a generalization of T-duality, called $T_2$-duality, that captures certain aspects of U-duality in M-theory. In particular, it features backgrounds that contain a 2-gerbe over a principal torus bundle, structures familiar from eleven-dimensional supergravity backgrounds. In special cases, it also incorporates S-duality in a precise sense. Our main result is a theorem characterizing $T_2$-dual pairs through spans of categorified principal bundles with connections, giving explicit rules for constructing a $T_2$-dual for a given background. A number of explicit examples illustrate how the various characteristic classes are mapped between the left and right backgrounds. For two-dimensional torus fibers, we also relate our construction to the combination of dimensional reduction and T-duality that links eleven-dimensional supergravity to type IIB supergravity. Finally, we discuss how $T_2$-duality arises from a Buscher-like span of 3d sigma models.
papers.summary: This paper extends T-duality to a new $T_2$-duality that incorporates 2-gerbes over torus bundles, providing a framework that unifies aspects of U- and S-duality in M-theory backgrounds. It characterizes dual pairs via spans of categorified principal 3-bundles with connections and demonstrates how characteristic classes map between dual geometries, including a link to the dimensional reduction from 11d supergravity to type IIB.

papers.title: Platonic self-dual solitons in a (1+1)-dimensional $\mathbb{CP}^1$ model
papers.authors: L. A. Ferreira, G. Marcelino
papers.abstract: We construct a family of self-dual $(1+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{CP}^1$ sigma models whose potentials $V$ are determined from pre-potentials $U$ by Platonic geometry. Using the round metric on $\mathbb{S}^2\simeq\mathbb{CP}^1$ and the generalized self-duality formalism, we build symmetry-invariant pre-potentials $U$ from the unit vertices of each Platonic solid intersecting the unit circumsphere. The regular-lattice sites associated with vertex, face-center, and edge-midpoint directions are critical points of $U$ and degenerate vacua of the scalar potential $V$. Dual solids share the same regular lattice but generate different pre-potentials, charges, potentials, and metric-gradient flows. Numerical integration reveals distinct self-dual trajectories and energy-density profiles, including multi-peak structures for paths passing near saddle points, while solutions with the same endpoint difference $\Delta U$ have the same total energy. The positive maxima of $V$ are also organized into symmetry orbits. This construction provides a geometric prescription for controlling the vacuum structure and self-dual sectors of $\mathbb{CP}^1$ models with a potential.
papers.summary: The authors construct a family of self-dual (1+1)-dimensional CP^1 sigma models whose scalar potentials are engineered from Platonic solid symmetries, yielding degenerate vacua at the vertices, face-centers, and edge-midpoints of the circumscribed sphere. Numerical analysis shows distinct self-dual trajectories and multi-peak energy densities, with total energy determined solely by the difference in pre-potential values between endpoints.

papers.title: Energy-energy correlators in the large-charge limit of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory
papers.authors: Alessandro Georgoudis, Max Jackson, Congkao Wen
papers.abstract: We study the energy-energy correlator (EEC) in heavy states of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory in the large-charge 't Hooft limit, in which the dimension $\Delta$ of the heavy operator (or, equivalently, its $R$-charge) is taken to infinity with the effective coupling $\lambda_Q \propto g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2\Delta$ held fixed. The relevant heavy-heavy-light-light four-point correlators are known to all orders in $\lambda_Q$ in this limit. For certain classes of operators, the perturbative series can be resummed to obtain exact finite-coupling expressions. We use these results to determine the corresponding EEC, whose dynamical part can be extracted from a double discontinuity of the four-point correlator. We determine the EEC at finite effective coupling and study its physical behavior as a function of $\lambda_Q$ and the angular separation between the detectors, both at generic angles and in the collinear and back-to-back limits.
papers.summary: The authors compute the energy-energy correlator for heavy operators in N=4 SYM in the large-charge limit, using all-order heavy-heavy-light-light four-point correlators and resummed perturbation theory to obtain exact finite-coupling results. They analyze the angular dependence of the EEC, including collinear and back-to-back regimes, revealing how the effective coupling controls the transition between weak and strong coupling behavior.

papers.title: A real superpotential for M-theory on eight-manifolds
papers.authors: Anthony Ashmore, Savdeep Sethi
papers.abstract: We study warped compactifications of eleven-dimensional supergravity on eight-manifolds to Minkowski or AdS vacua preserving $N=1$ supersymmetry in three dimensions. For backgrounds characterised by a local G$_2$ structure, we derive an off-shell real superpotential functional in terms of the internal geometry and fluxes without performing a finite Kaluza-Klein truncation. We obtain this expression in two independent ways: from the dimensional reduction of the gravitino variation and from the reduction of the eleven-dimensional gravitino action. We show that the critical-point equations, together with the vacuum value of the superpotential, are equivalent to the full set of supersymmetry conditions implied by the eleven-dimensional Killing spinor equations. When the local G$_2$ structure enhances to a global Spin(7) structure, our result reduces to the known superpotential for M-theory on Spin(7) manifolds.
papers.summary: The authors derive an off‑shell real superpotential for warped M‑theory compactifications on eight‑manifolds with local G$_2$ structure, expressed purely in terms of the internal geometry and fluxes. They show that the critical points of this functional reproduce the full set of supersymmetry conditions, and recover the known Spin(7) superpotential when the structure is global.

papers.title: Theory of Topologically Ordered Superfluids in 2+1 Dimensions
papers.authors: Chao-Ming Jian
papers.abstract: Topologically ordered superfluids (TOSFs) support deconfined, gapped anyonic excitations while remaining gapless because of Goldstone modes. We develop a general framework for characterizing their topological data in $(2+1)$-dimensional bosonic systems with spontaneously broken charge ${\rm U}(1)_{\rm c}$ symmetry. Gauging ${\rm U}(1)_{\rm c}$ maps a TOSF to a gapped topological order enriched by a dual ${\rm U}(1)_{\rm dual}$ symmetry with vanishing Hall conductance, while gauging ${\rm U}(1)_{\rm dual}$ recovers the TOSF. This two-way mapping allows the topological data of the TOSF, including the condensate charge, deconfined anyon content, and topological properties of vortices, to be systematically encoded using the algebraic framework of symmetry-enriched topological orders. In particular, superfluid vortices share the topological properties of flux defects associated with the residual discrete symmetry in the gapped anyon sector. We develop complementary algebraic and field-theoretic formulations of this framework, with the latter also suggesting a natural transition to a gapped topologically ordered phase. Additionally, using parton constructions, we present examples of TOSFs with non-Abelian vortices in bosonic systems.
papers.summary: This work introduces a systematic framework for describing topologically ordered superfluids in 2+1 dimensions, mapping them to symmetry-enriched topological orders via dual U(1) gauging. It also constructs explicit parton models yielding non-Abelian vortex excitations, offering a bridge between gapless superfluid Goldstone modes and gapped anyonic sectors.

papers.title: A Texture of Leptons for the Koide and Alikhanov relations
papers.authors: Alessandro Strumia
papers.abstract: Koide and Alikhanov proposed intriguing empirical relations among charged-lepton masses and neutrino mass splittings, respectively. We present mass-matrix textures that realise these relations and can jointly account for the observed lepton mixing angles, while yielding predictive correlations among them and the neutrino CP phases.
papers.summary: The paper constructs specific charged-lepton and neutrino mass matrices that simultaneously satisfy the Koide formula for charged leptons and the Alikhanov relation for neutrino mass splittings, while reproducing the observed PMNS mixing angles. It further derives testable correlations among mixing angles and CP-violating phases, offering a predictive framework for future neutrino experiments.

papers.title: pyAmpliCol: fast tree-level matrix elements
papers.authors: Rikkert Frederix, Valentin Hirschi, Lucien Huber, Shahriar Iravanian, Ben Ruijl, Timea Vitos
papers.abstract: Tree-level matrix elements sit at the heart of collider event generation, but their cost rises rapidly just where additional resolved radiation becomes most important. We present pyAmpliCol, a public generator aimed at extending the practical reach of colour-resolved matrix elements to higher multiplicities. It builds on the colour-ordered, off-shell-current strategy of AmpliCol, providing fast access to individual leading-colour flows while retaining the option of next-to-leading or exact full colour. The latter introduces its own high-multiplicity bottleneck: the dense interference of factorially many colour orderings. pyAmpliCol addresses this contraction with a fast Fourier transform on the symmetric group, preserving the exact colour result while avoiding the direct pairwise sum. Representative full-colour benchmarks demonstrate substantial speedups over the reference calculations considered here. It supports Standard Model processes and a broad class of UFO models, selected or summed helicities, vectorised evaluation and controllable numerical precision. It further provides colour- and spin-correlated Born quantities and tree-level colour connections at arbitrary perturbative order, opening the same framework to local subtraction and other higher-order applications. Together, these capabilities connect high-multiplicity matrix elements to their use in event generation, merging, parton showers and precision calculations within a single generator.
papers.summary: pyAmpliCol is a fast generator for tree‑level matrix elements that uses a Fourier‑transform based contraction to efficiently handle full colour interference at high multiplicities, enabling rapid evaluation of colour‑ and spin‑correlated Born terms for arbitrary perturbative order. It supports Standard Model and UFO models, vectorised evaluation, and precise control, making it useful for event generation, merging, parton showers, and higher‑order calculations.

papers.title: Gauging Modulated Symmetries: Bond Algebras, Higher-Form Symmetries, and Symmetry-Enriched Topological Order
papers.authors: Gustavo M. Yoshitome, Pedro R. S. Gomes, Guilherme Delfino
papers.abstract: We develop a constructive framework for characterizing modulated symmetries and their gauging in $d$-dimensional lattice systems. The modulation profiles are organized as a finite-dimensional representation of the space group acting on a finite Abelian internal symmetry group. Since the corresponding automorphism group is finite, the nontrivial spatial action factors through a finite quotient of the space group, leading to periodic modulation patterns and providing a classification framework for discrete Abelian modulated symmetries. The symmetry-allowed local interactions are systematically obtained from a kernel construction, which also yields an algebra of open operators. Upon gauging, its elements are transmuted into extended Wilson and boundary operators while retaining their algebraic relations. In the deconfined regime, the resulting algebra realizes a mixed 't Hooft anomaly, providing a microscopic route to Abelian crystalline symmetry-enriched topological phases (SETs). These SETs do not mix electric and magnetic sectors, which transform in mutually contragredient representations, thereby preserving their braiding pairing. We illustrate the framework through explicit examples and show that several models present in the literature fit naturally within our construction.
papers.summary: The paper presents a systematic construction for modulated symmetries in lattice systems, showing how finite Abelian internal symmetries with space‑group modulation can be gauged to produce mixed ’t Hooft anomalies and crystalline SET phases. It develops a kernel‑based method to derive symmetry‑allowed interactions and the resulting algebra of Wilson and boundary operators, illustrating the framework with explicit lattice models.

papers.title: Equal-mass sunset integrals and genus-zero local Gromov--Witten theory of Calabi--Yau $n$-folds
papers.authors: Hartmut Maennel, Pierre Vanhove
papers.abstract: We prove an exact identity, as convergent logarithmic germs at large Euclidean momentum, between the equal-mass two-dimensional $(n-1)$-loop sunset Feynman integral, with $n\geq4$, and the genus-zero one-point descendant invariants of the local Calabi--Yau $n$-fold $X_n=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_n})$, where $F_n\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{n}$ is a smooth $(1,\ldots,1)$ hypersurface. Writing $s$ for the momentum variable and $y=-1/s$, the identity reads $$   I^{(n-1)}_{\circleddash}(s)=(-1)^{n-1}yA\,\Bigl[nR^{n-1}-\theta_Q{\mathcal D}_0^\Delta\,R^{n-2}   +\sum_{j=0}^{n-3}c_jR^j\Bigr], $$ where $R=\log y+O(y)$ is the local mirror coordinate, $A=\theta_yR$, $Q=e^R$, ${\mathcal D}_0^\Delta(Q)$ is the primary one-point potential, and each $c_j$ is an explicit linear combination of $1$, the descendant series ${\mathcal D}_a^\Delta(Q)$ and their derivatives $\theta_Q{\mathcal D}_a^\Delta$, $0\leq a\leq n-2$, with coefficients in the odd-zeta values $\mathbb Q[\zeta(3),\zeta(5),\ldots]$ coming from the Gamma class. The descendant series are given explicitly by the ambient hypergeometric series and the inverse mirror map. We also prove global univalence of the principal mirror map, with explicit upper and lower bounds on the $Q$-Taylor radii, extract the full primary evaluation divisor and its integral cover transform, and reduce the ambient endpoint constants to a finite universal Gamma-class part and $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ real parameters.
papers.summary: This paper establishes an exact correspondence between equal‑mass sunset Feynman integrals in (n‑1) loops and genus‑zero Gromov‑Witten invariants of a local Calabi‑Yau n‑fold, providing explicit hypergeometric expressions and mirror‑map univalence. It offers new analytic tools for evaluating multi‑loop integrals via mirror symmetry, but does not directly address holography, celestial amplitudes, or p‑adic aspects.

papers.title: Hamiltonian framework for Chiral Gauge Theories on a Disk Boundary
papers.authors: Srimoyee Sen
papers.abstract: I propose a Hamiltonian framework for chiral gauge theories (CGT) based on a Euclidean formulation which uses 2n dimensional chiral fermions on the boundary of a 2n+1 dimensional disk. In the original Euclidean formulation, boundary gauge fields were extended into the bulk using $2n + 1$ dimensional gauge field equations of motion (EOM) which creates a bottleneck for constructing a Hamiltonian.
